newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan bourse queries suspected rule violators.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan bourse queries suspected rule violators.

text.p: Pakistan's main Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) said on Tuesday it asked 68 listed companies, most of them in the textile sector, to explain various apparent violations of listing rules within seven days.
The violations included delays in holding annual general meetings for the last three years and not declaring dividends for five years, a KSE executive said.

Action taken if the violators failed to adequately explain the lapses could include a suspension of trading in the companies' shares, said the executive, who did not want to be identified. The companies were not named.
Several textile mills have been declared sick and closed owing to heavy losses caused by high domestic cotton prices, one stockbroker said.
The KSE has 783 listed companies with a listed capital of 204.45 billion rupees and a market capitalisation of 467.65 billion rupees, the KSE executive said.
